stories.title: Sports Tech Firm Genius Sports Moves U.S. HQ to Vornado’s 1290 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Sports analytics and technology company Genius Sports is relocating its U.S. headquarters to 1290 Avenue of the Americas. The London-based company’s new 10-year lease with landlord Vornado Realty Trust spans 53,000 square feet across part of the tower’s sixth floor. Asking rent was $99 per square foot, according to The Real Deal, which first reported on the lease. Newmark’s Josh Berg and A.J. Dorn negotiated the deal on behalf of Genius Sports, while Vornado was represented in-house by Ryan Levy and Edward Riguardi. A spokesperson for the landlord declined to comment on the transaction. The deal offers Genius Sports a marked expansion from its 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea offices at 512 West 22nd Street. That building changed hands last year from Vornado and the Albanese Organization to Raghsa Real Estate for $205 million. Genius Sports’ arrival brings 1290 Avenue of the Americas to 95 percent occupancy. The 43-story, full-block building between 51st and 52nd streets is anchored by investment management firm Neuberger Berman, and recently underwent a $45 million renovation that updated lobby and building amenities. Vornado owns 70 percent of the building, while the Trump Organization holds a passive 30 percent stake. Other recent arrivals at the tower include business consulting firms Portage Point Partners and Protiviti, which CO reported leased a total of 93,000 square feet late last year. In January, investment manager Oaktree leased the building’s entire 12th floor, just a few stories below law firm Selendy Gay’s 101,000-square-foot offices. Spokespeople for Genius Sports and Newmark did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Genius Sports relocates U.S. HQ to 1290 Avenue of the Americas, 53K SF, $99/SF asking rent
Lease brings building to 95% occupancy; tenant doubles from 28K SF West Chelsea office
London-based sports tech firm signals Manhattan office market demand from growth-stage tech employers
stories.summary: Genius Sports, a London-based sports analytics firm, signed a 10-year lease for 53,000 square feet at Vornado's 1290 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan at $99/SF asking rent. The move represents a near-doubling of the company's NYC footprint from its previous 28K SF West Chelsea location. The lease brings the 43-story tower to 95% occupancy.
stories.impact: Tech and financial services tenant demand remains robust in Midtown Manhattan despite office sector headwinds, underpinning trophy-asset rents and occupancy. However, this signals continued flight to quality Class A office—not broad sector recovery—and reinforces that multifamily developers should monitor Midtown/Plaza District job growth (finance, tech, professional services) as a leading indicator of residential demand in nearby submarkets like Hell's Kitchen, Tribeca, and Upper East Side.

stories.title: SJC Ventures Sells Whole Foods-Anchored Center in South Florida for $83M
stories.excerpt: SJC Ventures has sold a newly completed Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Fla., for $83 million, property records show. Called Doral Marketplace, the property spans 89,000 square feet at 10800 Northwest 41st Street, about a mile east of the Florida Turnpike and 14 miles west of Downtown Miami. Atlanta-based SJC Ventures completed the 10-acre strip mall last quarter. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre portion of the property leased to Chick-fil-A. Records list the buyer as Traditions Management, a Dallas-based developer and operator of senior living communities. The buyer assumed a loan with $50 million in outstanding debt, which has now been assigned to the Bank of Texas. Whole Foods is Doral Marketplace’s biggest tenant with a 43,000-square-foot location. Other tentants include J. Crew Factory, Ulta Beauty, Shake Shack, First Watch, GoodVets, The Spot Barbershop, Encore Nails, VIO MedSpa and Apizza Brooklyn Resto + Vino. The sale comes as Miami-Dade County retail leasing remains strong. During the second quarter of 2026, average asking rents jumped to $42.50 per square foot, up 2.6 percent quarter-over-quarter, while the vacancy rate fell to 3 percent. More than 1.3 million square feet of retail space remains under construction, including another Whole Foods location in South Beach, for which developer Russell Galbut nabbed a $54 million construction loan last year. Representatives for SJC Ventures and Traditions Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SJC Ventures sells Whole Foods-anchored Doral Marketplace to Traditions Management for $83M
Retail center spans 89K SF; buyer assumes $50M loan, paid $33M equity
Miami-Dade County Q2 2026 retail asking rents hit $42.50/SF, +2.6% YoY growth
stories.summary: SJC Ventures sold Doral Marketplace, a newly completed 89,000-square-foot Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Florida, for $83 million to Traditions Management, a Dallas-based senior living developer. The buyer assumed $50 million in debt; the sale excluded an adjacent 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A pad. Miami-Dade County retail rents accelerated to $42.50/SF in Q2 2026, up 2.6% year-over-year.
stories.impact: Strong retail leasing momentum and rent growth in West Dade/Doral signals robust local consumer demand and population health in the corridor. For multifamily developers, this validates growing residential demand in outer-ring Dade County suburbs (Doral, Medley, Tamarac areas) as white-collar and service workers seek affordability near job clusters; pipeline of new retail and entertainment anchors supports case for apartment construction in these submarkets.

stories.title: KeyBank Expands to 113K SF at Elecor’s 1301 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: A major banking institution has added 15,292 square feet to its Manhattan office footprint, Commercial Observer has learned. Keybank signed a 15-year deal to renew its existing space and expand to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties’ 1301 Avenue of the Americas across the entire 35th, 36th and 37th floors, as well as portions of the 28th and 38th floors, according to the landlord. Asking rent for the Plaza District office tower was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the second quarter of 2026 was $86.18 per square foot, according to a report from CBRE. “As KeyBank continues to grow and adapt to the evolving needs of our business, we remain focused on providing our employees with an environment that fosters collaboration and connection,” John Manginelli, Hudson Valley and metro New York market president at KeyBank, said in a statement. “Expanding our footprint at 1301 Avenue of the Americas enables us to support that vision while positioning us for continued growth and enhanced service to our clients across the region.” JLL’s Matthew Astrachan, Justin Haber, Kyle Riker, Adam Hill and Bob Beckstedt represented KeyBank in the transaction, while Peter Brindley, Douglas Neye and Sean Kirk handled negotiations in-house for Elecor Properties. “This was a highly strategic transaction that addressed several priorities at once: securing more space for KeyBank’s growing businesses, keeping its teams together within one elevator bank, creating the opportunity to upgrade the existing workplace, and establishing a true New York City headquarters with prominent signage,” Astrachan said in a statement. Other tenants in the building between West 52nd and West 53rd streets include investment bank Piper Sandler, which signed a lease for 140,000 square feet in August 2025, back when Elecor was still Paramount Group. bullets: KeyBank expands to 112.9K SF at Elecor's 1301 Avenue of the Americas, 15-year renewal
Occupies entire 35th, 36th, 37th floors plus portions of 28th and 38th
Midtown office asking rent averaged $86.18/SF in Q2 2026; bank grows NYC footprint
stories.summary: KeyBank signed a 15-year lease to renew and expand to 112,924 square feet at 1301 Avenue of the Americas in Manhattan's Plaza District, occupying the entire 35th, 36th, and 37th floors plus portions of the 28th and 38th. Midtown office asking rents averaged $86.18/SF in Q2 2026. KeyBank's statement emphasized employee collaboration and growth positioning.
stories.impact: Major regional bank expansion in Midtown signals sustained financial services employment growth in Manhattan, supporting baseline office demand and indirectly apartment demand among white-collar workers in surrounding residential markets (Midtown South, Turtle Bay, Roosevelt Island). However, this is a renewal with modest net-new space; true multifamily signal would emerge if KeyBank expands headcount materially or if competing banks similarly backfill leased space, confirming finance sector stabilization post-rates.

stories.title: League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space
stories.excerpt: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on the $78 million mixed-use business park Lilac Field in League City. The development is seeking its first industrial and retail tenants. Located between League City Parkway and SH 146, Lilac Field will span 24.5 acres and include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space. Community Impact reports once complete, Lilac Field will include 16 small warehouse units and seven retail and restaurant buildings, with warehouse tenants expected to include entertainment venues, gyms, childcare providers and breweries. The development’s first two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027. The developer is seeking industrial clients, such as aerospace and aviation suppliers, marine service groups, technology firms, energy service companies, advanced manufacturing users and specialty distributors to rent its warehouse space. The full buildout is projected to take three to five years. The post League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alexander Grene Development breaks ground on $78M mixed-use Lilac Field in League City, TX
Project includes 70K SF retail/restaurant and 220K SF flexible warehouse on 24.5 acres
First two industrial buildings due early 2027; targets aerospace, aviation, tech, marine tenants
stories.summary: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on Lilac Field, a $78 million mixed-use business park in League City, Texas spanning 24.5 acres with 70,000 square feet of retail/restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse. The development includes 16 small warehouse units and seven retail buildings; first industrial deliveries expected early 2027. Target tenants include aerospace/aviation suppliers, marine service groups, and advanced manufacturing.
stories.impact: League City's diversification into light industrial, entertainment, and tech-adjacent uses reflects strong population and employment growth in the Houston-Galveston corridor, driving secondary market demand for workforce housing. Multifamily developers should monitor Lilac Field and similar industrial-retail mixed-use projects in League City/Pearland as leading indicators of near-term demand for Class B/C apartments for warehouse and service workers; proximity to SH 146 and League City Parkway increases commute accessibility.

stories.title: Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Developer Naseem Shaik is moving forward on a $240 million Prosper project that will include a hotel, offices, retail and restaurants. No multifamily is planned at the time. Dubbed Bella Prosper, it will sit on 61 acres with a large manmade lake in the middle. The development will incorporate one-story offices as well as office space above restaurant and retail spaces. Features of Bella Prosper include a 139-key hotel geared toward business travelers, a public parking deck and a park with a water feature. Bella Prosper is slated to build at least 60,950 square feet of retail space. Community Impact reports Bella Prosper is expected to create $59.8 million in annual taxable sales. Developers estimate that Bella Prosper as a whole will generate $88.3 million in net benefits for the town over the next 25 years. Construction on Phase 1 was originally expected to start in late 2027. The post Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Naseem Shaik plans $240M Bella Prosper mixed-use project on 61 acres in Prosper, TX
Includes 139-key hotel, office, 60.9K SF retail, no multifamily; Phase 1 target late 2027
Project estimated to generate $88.3M net benefits to town over 25 years
stories.summary: Developer Naseem Shaik is advancing Bella Prosper, a $240 million mixed-use development on 61 acres in Prosper, Texas, featuring a 139-key business hotel, office space, 60,950 square feet of retail, restaurants, and a public park with water feature. No multifamily component is currently planned. Phase 1 construction was originally slated for late 2027; the project is projected to generate $88.3 million in net town benefits over 25 years.
stories.impact: Prosper's mixed-use office-hotel-retail growth signals Dallas North employment hub maturation and attractions for business travelers and office workers, likely increasing residential demand nearby. However, the developer's deliberate exclusion of multifamily is notable—it suggests either land constraints, zoning limitations, or a competitive multifamily market in Prosper already well-served by nearby supply, indicating a saturated submarket; multifamily developers should validate absorption and rent trends in Prosper before entering.

stories.title: Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets
stories.excerpt: The U.S. commercial real estate recovery is following markedly different paths across property sectors and markets, Integra Realty Resources (IRR) said in its newly released 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report. More than 90% of retail markets surveyed are in recovery or expansion, while office markets remain evenly divided between recovery and recession. Multifamily performance is shaped largely by local supply cycles, while industrial markets are concentrated primarily in the expansion and hypersupply phases. Across all four sectors, IRR’s data show a continued flight to quality, with modern, well-located and specialized properties outperforming older or commodity-oriented assets. Meanwhile, speculative construction has slowed sharply. “National data provide essential context, but the clearest picture emerges when it is informed by what is happening on the ground,” said IRR CEO Anthony M. Graziano. “Investors cannot assume that modest rate cuts will meaningfully improve transaction economics, particularly while long-term borrowing costs and equity return requirements remain elevated. Through year-end and into 2027, we expect opportunities to remain concentrated in markets and assets where the basis, income growth and local demand support the investment case.” The post Retail Leads as CRE Recovery Diverges Across Sectors, Markets appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Integra Realty Resources 2026 mid-year report: 90% of retail markets in recovery/expansion
Office markets split evenly between recovery and recession; multifamily shaped by local supply cycles
Across all sectors, flight to quality persists; speculative construction slowed sharply
stories.summary: Integra Realty Resources' 2026 Mid-Year Viewpoint Report shows marked divergence across CRE sectors: over 90% of retail markets are in recovery or expansion, while office markets remain evenly split between recovery and recession. Multifamily performance is driven primarily by local supply cycles and industrial is concentrated in expansion/hypersupply. All sectors exhibit a flight to quality, with modern, well-located, and specialized assets outperforming commodities. Speculative construction has slowed sharply.
stories.impact: This macro snapshot confirms that multifamily success depends entirely on local market supply-demand dynamics, not national trends—underwriting rigor on site-specific absorption, competing pipeline, and demographic inflows is non-negotiable. The pullback in speculative construction suggests rising cost of capital and lender caution; developers with strong capital access and basis can acquire distressed/shovel-ready deals from forced sellers or underwriters. Flight to quality also signals that Class A/trophy multifamily with modern amenities and premier locations will outperform B/C; consider repositioning or value-add strategies in secondary markets with supply constraints.

stories.title: Mac Cosmetics’ SoHo Flagship Relocates to 5K SF at 579 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Mac Cosmetics has selected a new foundation in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The global makeup brand signed a 5,325-square-foot lease at 579 Broadway between Prince and East Houston streets to host its next flagship location in the trendy shopping corridor, according to an announcement from landlord broker Newmark. The deal represents a relocation of just two blocks from Mac’s current perch alongside Bloomingdale’s at 506 Broadway. The landlord at 579 Broadway, Lord Shivas Properties, was represented by Newmark’s Ariel Schuster, Michael Paster and Logan Ryan. Paster said in a statement that the location, neighbored by brands like jewelry brand Pandora and bohemian clothing store Free People Movement, was a “natural fit for Mac Cosmetics.” The brand plans to occupy approximately 3,825 square feet on the ground floor and 1,500 square feet of lower-level space within the five-story building. The length of Mac’s lease and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from CBRE found retail rents near SoHo’s Prince Street averaged $1,408 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. Mac will take possession of the storefront in January, according to Newmark. Its current occupant, British fashion retailer AllSaints, will occupy the space through the end of the year. A spokesperson for AllSaints did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its future plans in the neighborhood. Cushman & Wakefield’s Mike O’Neill, Jason Greenstone and Taylor Reynolds negotiated the lease on behalf of Mac Cosmetics. The lease offered Mac the opportunity to secure a highly visible location in the corridor, O’Neill told CO in a statement. “We’re pleased to have helped facilitate a transaction that aligns Mac with a location well positioned to support its long-term retail objectives,” O’Neill said. Lord Shivas Properties also owns the lot’s adjacent storefront at 152 Mercer Street, the site of luxury knitwear brand Extreme Cashmere‘s U.S. flagship. Emily
bullets: Mac Cosmetics relocates SoHo flagship to 5.3K SF at 579 Broadway, two blocks east
Lease includes 3.8K SF ground floor and 1.5K SF lower level; neighbors Pandora, Free People
Move reflects continued retail vitality in SoHo corridor despite broader urban retail consolidation
stories.summary: Mac Cosmetics signed a lease for 5,325 square feet at 579 Broadway in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, relocating its flagship approximately two blocks from its current location at 506 Broadway alongside Bloomingdale's. The space includes 3,825 SF ground floor and 1,500 SF lower-level retail within a five-story building. The brand joins nearby tenants Pandora and Free People Movement in the trendy shopping corridor.
stories.impact: Continued flagship retail consolidation and relocation within SoHo indicates landlord competition for premium tenants and tenant optimization of customer traffic corridors; rents and occupancy remain resilient in trophy shopping districts. Multifamily developers should note that SoHo's retail-dining-entertainment ecosystem continues to anchor high rents and desirability for surrounding residential, supporting case for luxury/Class A apartment development in nearby Hudson Square, NoLita, and lower Manhattan if zoning and land availability permit; this micro-market remains demand-insulated vs. broader Manhattan softness.

stories.title: Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms
stories.excerpt: The building is nearly a 100 years old, but that isn’t stopping Phoenix developers CivicGroup and Sunflower Development from converting the onetime office tower into hotel rooms. Built in 1928, the Security Building will undergo a $135 million renovation that will include 255 hotel rooms. In addition to the hotel rooms, the redevelopment will include 15,000 square feet of meeting space – including the 5,500-square-foot 1928 ballroom – and other amenities. The investor duo hopes to open five food-and-beverage outlets in the hotel, including multiple bars, a three-meal restaurant, and an upscale eatery. The building is currently owned by Maricopa County and will continue to lease the building to the development team as a hotel for at least 20 years. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the project requires a significant amount of preservation work – including the removal of drywall, carpet, non-historic walls and cubicles. The developers hope to start in the first quarter of 2027 and open in Q4 2028. The post Vintage Phoenix Midrise Office Building Slated for Hotel Rooms appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CivicGroup and Sunflower Development convert 1928 Security Building to 255-room hotel, $135M reno
Building owned by Maricopa County; 20+ year lease-to-own by developers starting Q1 2027
Historic office-to-hospitality conversion reflects Phoenix downtown revitalization and visitor demand
stories.summary: Phoenix-based developers CivicGroup and Sunflower Development are converting the historic 1928 Security Building into a 255-room hotel with $135 million in renovation. The project includes 15,000 SF of meeting space, a 5,500 SF historic ballroom, and five F&B outlets. The building is owned by Maricopa County; developers will operate under a long-term lease starting Q1 2027, targeting opening in Q4 2028.
stories.impact: Downtown Phoenix office-to-hotel conversion signals weak office occupancy fundamentals and developer confidence in tourism/hospitality recovery over traditional office demand. For multifamily developers, this underscores that Phoenix's CBD is shifting toward hospitality and mixed-use entertainment rather than office density, tilting residential demand toward suburban/fringe markets (Scottsdale, Tempe, Gilbert) where renters seek walkable, amenity-rich neighborhoods near employment centers outside downtown. Avoid competing for downtown office-conversion residential plays; focus on transit-oriented or suburban mixed-use projects instead.

stories.title: Law Firm DLA Piper, Insurance Group Ascot Ink Deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Two office tenants at Mitsui Fudosan America’s 1251 Avenue of the Americas are extending or expanding their footprints, Commercial Observer has learned. Law firm DLA Piper expanded by 41,600 square feet on the entire 29th floor of the Midtown building with an 8.5-year term, bringing the law firm to a total of 210,000 square feet at the property between West 49th and West 50th streets. Meanwhile, insurance company Ascot Group signed a 12-year extension for its 44,100-square-foot offices on the entire 43rd floor, according to sources familiar with the deal. Ascot was previously subleasing the space. Asking rent for Ascot’s space was $150 per square foot, while the asking rent for DLA Piper’s deal was $140 per square foot, according to the source. Newmark‘s David Falk, Pete Shimkin, Eric Cagner and Claire Koeppel are exclusive leasing agents for the 54-story office tower, but declined to comment. CBRE‘s John Nugent and Alexander Golod negotiated on behalf of Ascot, while a separate CBRE team of Mike Wellen and Ken Rapp handled the deal for DLA Piper. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the DLA Piper deal and declined to comment on Ascot. Other recent deals at 1251 Avenue of the Americas include a 41,600-square-foot lease for alternative investing firm LGT Capital Partners in May and an expansion to 80,200 square feet for Trust Company of the West in November 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: DLA Piper expands 41.6K SF to 210K SF total at 1251 Avenue of the Americas, $140/SF
Ascot Group extends 44.1K SF insurance offices 12-year term at $150/SF on entire 43rd floor
Both deals signal sustained Midtown Plaza District demand from corporate tenants; asking rents remain elevated
stories.summary: Law firm DLA Piper expanded by 41,600 square feet on the entire 29th floor of Mitsui Fudosan America's 1251 Avenue of the Americas under an 8.5-year lease at $140/SF, bringing its total occupancy to 210,000 square feet. Insurance company Ascot Group concurrently signed a 12-year extension for 44,100 square feet on the entire 43rd floor at $150/SF, converting from a prior sublease arrangement.
stories.impact: Back-to-back expansions by major corporate tenants (law firm and insurance) in Plaza District Midtown validate sustained demand from anchor service-sector employers, underpinning office fundamentals and indirectly supporting nearby residential. However, both deals involve existing tenants rather than new-to-market entrants; true demand signal would be new corporate HQ relocations or openings. For multifamily: continued Midtown white-collar employment justifies continued investment in class-A residential near transit (Hudson Yards, Midtown South); monitor if current $140–150/SF office rents decline—a trigger for office-to-residential conversions.

stories.title: Value Defines Success for Dining Industry in 2026
stories.excerpt: Value has become a defining theme across the dining industry, yet the definition of value can vary across the sector’s diverse restaurant categories and for individual brands, Placer.ai says in a new white paper. A closer look at chains across the industry suggests that, amid ongoing economic pressure, perceptions of value are evolving. Titled Dining In 2026: All Roads Lead To Value, the white paper says that consumers in 2026 appear to be evaluating value through a broader lens that includes experience, quality, convenience and affordability. While overall dining traffic this year has trailed 2025 in most months, some segments are doing better than others, such as fast casual and fine dining. Fast casual in particular has seen a number of dining chains maintaining positive traffic momentum by pairing everyday value with the benefits of full-service dining, reports Placer.ai. Chipotle, for example, has achieved success by pairing menu novelty with loyalty perks to reinforce a value proposition anchored by quality and experience The post Value Defines Success for Dining Industry in 2026 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Placer.ai white paper: 2026 dining traffic trails 2025 in most months; value perception broadening
Fast casual and fine dining outperform; Chipotle sustains momentum via novelty and loyalty perks
Consumers now evaluate value via experience, quality, convenience, affordability—not price alone
stories.summary: Placer.ai's 2026 white paper, 'Dining In 2026: All Roads Lead To Value,' finds that overall dining traffic has trailed 2025 in most months, yet value perceptions are evolving beyond pure affordability to include experience, quality, and convenience. Fast casual and fine dining segments are outperforming; Chipotle, for example, has maintained positive traffic by pairing menu innovation with loyalty programs.
stories.impact: Dining traffic weakness and bifurcation between fast casual/fine dining suggests middle-market casual dining is under pressure while price-value and premium experience categories thrive. For multifamily developers, this informs amenity and retail ground-floor strategy: include fast casual (Chipotle, Sweetgreen) and high-end dining/bars in mixed-use projects to drive leasing and NOI; avoid mid-tier sit-down casual concepts. Additionally, softening overall dining traffic may signal cautious consumer sentiment on discretionary spending, which could temper rent growth assumptions in new markets; validate local employment and wage trends before underwriting aggressive rent escalation.
